_id: best rung 2/5: the SINGLE-ASSET STACK at the LOW band. Identical to best001 except that the 24.125/5.800 GHz pair is replaced by freq009's 2.450/0.915 GHz pair. It exists because the frozen sweep does not agree with itself about which band wins: freq012 has the best RUN-WIDE position (2.2758 m against freq009's 2.3991) while freq009 has the best TAIL (1.1149 m against freq012's 1.2310). One of those is the number a mission would be sized on and the other is the number a convergence plot shows.
_delta: signals only -> freq009's 2.450 GHz / 915 MHz ISM pair. Product interval, ground oscillator and every error source inherited from best001.
_whyTHISbandMATTERSbeyondTHENUMBER: The two bands are separated by 26x in carrier frequency and the run-wide difference between them is 5%. If that holds under stacking, band selection for THIS system is not an accuracy argument at all and can be decided on the arguments that actually differ: 24 GHz carries roughly 0.2 dB/km of gaseous absorption against 0.01 at 2.45 GHz, needs a far tighter pointing budget, and -- measured on carr005 -- charges the carrier 0.483 cycles of noise against 0.035 at L1, which removes any prospect of integer ambiguity resolution. The 915 MHz / 2.45 GHz pair gives up 5% of run-wide position and takes all of that back.
_theCONDITIONINGARGUMENT: The freq axis result is that the ionosphere/geometry separation is driven by |1-(fp/fs)^2|: 16.3 for the 24.125/5.8 pair, 6.17 for 2.45/0.915, and 0.647 for the L1/L2 pair the golden carries. Both ISM pairs are an order better conditioned than L1/L2 and the difference between them is the second-order effect this rung prices.
